reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume has sustained a ~2x increase since August 2026, from a ~600/month baseline to 1180-1260/month (E-06). The majority of disputed bills (1,785 of 3,025) were issued on ACTUAL meter reads, not ESTIMATED ones (E-02), and no tariff change occurred (E-03), so the dominant driver is an unisolated billing-accuracy defect in the billing import/validation step affecting ACTUAL-read bills, not primarily the estimate-substitution pathway (field route completion fell to 0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-01, which can only explain the smaller ESTIMATED-read share); ticket response handling itself remains within SLA (E-04), ruling out a handling-capacity cause.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: CRM dispute volume sustained a ~2x increase from a ~600/month baseline (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-06). Of the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (41% of 3,025 disputed bills, E-02), 1,184 (95.5%) trace to billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, rejecting valid AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12) because BV-17 compares raw register values with no unit scaling (E-13) against meters on v4.2 firmware, which records readings in 0.1 m3 units instead of the plain m3 units v3.x firmware uses (E-14) - a mismatch that makes normal consumption appear ~10x higher than the 12-month m3 history BV-17 checks against. This BV-17 unit-scaling defect is the best-evidenced mechanism for the ESTIMATED-read dispute pathway; whether it also explains the larger ACTUAL-read disputed-bill share (59%, 1,785/3,025, E-02) is untested and tracked separately.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
